historical_hard_anchors: Shinhoto was already in prewar/early-war conversion and entered combat in the Philippines in spring 1942.
A widely used production series gives 503 new Shinhoto in '1942', but the exact calendar-vs-fiscal basis is not trusted for event dating.
About 300 older 57mm Type97 tanks were rebuilt with the new turret over the transition.
Type1 mobile 47mm AT-gun production at Nagoya Arsenal began in April 1942; tank gun and towed gun are related but physically distinct products.
Ho-Ni I program began in 1941 and historical series production is about 26 vehicles in 1942.

47mm_resource_wallet.finding: The towed Type1 47mm and the Type1 47mm tank gun share ammunition/metallurgy/design ecosystem but are not one identical barrel/assembly line. Towed-gun output therefore does not subtract one-for-one from tank-gun output.
47mm_resource_wallet.tank_gun_constraint: Final barrel machining, breech/recoil hardware, sights and turret integration remain real constraints.
47mm_resource_wallet.branch_effect: Earlier 68-hull conversion experience + tighter acceptance/QC can front-load retrofit throughput, but cannot double it.
47mm_resource_wallet.reason_for_band: Enough to exploit existing turret program without assuming undocumented 1942 tank-gun surge. If later Osaka/Sagami gun records show lower throughput, retrofit count slides first.

calendar_1942_event_curve_working.explanation: Early months must support a March training/shipping detachment; later 1942 is the mass-conversion period. Numbers are a dated Branch model, while the frequently quoted 503 remains a source-series anchor rather than a literal calendar total.

1942_national_AFV_policy.total_output: Keep national tracked-AFV envelope close to historical-equivalent. Do not cash Branch steel improvement directly into extra tank hulls.
1942_national_AFV_policy.main_change: Model mix and retrofit/acceptance speed, plus recovery/workshop assets.
1942_national_AFV_policy.HaGo: Keep high production/availability; southern success and better reliability reduce urgency of Ke-Ni replacement.

HoNiI.guard: Any amount above historical-equivalent consumes Type97 chassis + Type90 75mm gun resources.

ChiHe.branch_effect: Testing and welding/process closure improve, but successful Shinhoto makes a crash line switch unattractive.

Philippines.historical_anchor: A specially trained Shinhoto detachment left Japan around 20 Mar 1942 and reached the Philippines around the end of March; two Shinhoto are firmly associated with the Corregidor landing after-action imagery/records.
Philippines.branch: Earlier accepted stock makes a slightly larger training/issue detachment physically possible, but size is NOT changed until transport/landing-craft and crew records are audited.
Philippines.strategic_outcome: No automatic change to the already-decided fall of Bataan/Corregidor.

Malaya.branch: No retroactive replacement before campaign close centered. 57mm HE remains valuable and invasion shipping/OOB was fixed.

Burma.branch: Potential 47mm reinforcement must be traced through actual 2nd/14th Tank Regiment logistics; no automatic presence.

Manchuria_China.branch: Primary destination for 1942 re-equipment as 1st/2nd Tank Divisions form in Manchuria and 3rd Tank Division is formed in China late 1942.

end_1942_working_state.Shinhoto_transition: Far enough advanced that 47mm is the normal new medium-tank standard; old 57mm vehicles remain deliberately useful in infantry-support/gun-tank roles.

retrofit_cumulative.remaining_of_about_300_historical_rebuil: roughly 50-100 vehicles, to be resolved in 1943

not_granted: all Southern Army units converted to Shinhoto

next_required: Reconstruct calendar/fiscal 1943 from factory/acceptance sources rather than reusing annual table blindly.
Resolve Chi-He: calendar 1943 pre-series vs FY1943 Feb-Mar 1944 production.
Resolve Ke-Ni 1943 new-build vs repair classification.
Bind 3rd Tank Division + Five-Go demand to actual model mix and repair/recovery wallet.
Then propagate GALVANIC M4 shock into 75mm stopgap requirement timing.
